name: coven-mcp
summary: An MCP server that bridges the Coven daemon to any stdio-capable MCP client.

quirks.detail: Requests are camelCase and session records reply snake_case, but the events envelope is camelCase (events, nextCursor, hasMore) while its event objects stay snake_case.
Event payload_json is a JSON string requiring a second parse.
A fifth event kind 'kill' exists alongside output, input, status, exit.
GET /sessions returns a bare array without pagination params and an envelope with them; GET /memory always returns a bare array.
Health advertises string capabilities such as eventCursor: 'sequence', so a truthiness check would wrongly grant permission.
The daemon reports covenVersion '0.0.0' even on a 0.0.34 install, so gating must use apiVersion and capabilities.

modules.role: Process entrypoint. Resolves the socket path, parses the allowlist, fails fast on misconfiguration, wires the stdio transport, and handles SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown.
Registers all nine MCP tools, validates inputs before any I/O, applies the health and allowlist gates, and shapes every result or structured error.
Parses COVEN_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS, canonicalizes roots through symlinks, and enforces path-component containment. Fails the process on any invalid entry.
Handshake gate run before every non-health call. Requires ok, the exact api version, and the named capability as literal true. Caches for 1.5s, single-flight.
HTTP over Unix socket. Connect and response timeouts, 4 MiB caps in both directions, abort propagation, and mapping of daemon error envelopes to structured errors.
The single snake_case to camelCase boundary. Normalizes sessions, harness manifests, acks, and memory entries, and applies the memory excerpt redaction policy.
Bounded polling reader. Drains pages, guards against cursor regression, enforces byte/page/event/time budgets, and returns exactly one documented stop tuple.
Streaming terminal state machine. Strips ANSI/C0/C1 sequences, applies carriage-return overwrite, and exports compacted parser state so resumes are lossless.
HMAC-SHA-256 signed continuation tokens over UTF-16LE pending state, bound to a session id, size-capped, and constant-time verified.
The CovenMcpError type and the closed set of eleven error codes every failure maps onto.

tools.name: coven_health
tools.notes: Never returns a tool error; an unreachable daemon is reported in the result body.

tools.name: coven_list_harnesses
tools.notes: May disclose absolute harness manifest paths.

tools.name: coven_list_sessions
tools.notes: Normalizes both the bare array and the paginated envelope.

tools.name: coven_read_output
tools.notes: Bounded polling with signed resume tokens; the project's most complex component.

tools.name: coven_list_memory
tools.notes: A file lister, not search. Excerpts blank unless explicitly enabled.

tools.name: coven_start_session
tools.notes: Canonicalizes projectRoot and cwd; requires cwd inside projectRoot.

tools.name: coven_send_input
tools.notes: Fetches the authoritative record first. Data is forwarded verbatim; no newline appended.

requestLifecycle.name: Schema validation
requestLifecycle.detail: zod shape plus explicit byte, charset, and range checks. Failures return INVALID_INPUT before any I/O.

requestLifecycle.name: Health and capability gate
requestLifecycle.detail: ok === true, apiVersion === coven.daemon.v1, required capability strictly true. 1.5s single-flight cache.

requestLifecycle.name: Authorization
requestLifecycle.detail: Write tools only. Canonicalize, then path-component containment. Input and kill authorize the daemon's own record.

requestLifecycle.name: Transport
requestLifecycle.detail: HTTP over the Unix socket with timeouts, 4 MiB caps, and abort propagation.

requestLifecycle.name: Normalization or output pipeline
requestLifecycle.detail: JSON becomes stable camelCase; PTY event streams are sanitized and tokenized.

requestLifecycle.name: Result shaping
requestLifecycle.detail: One JSON text content item, or isError with a structured CovenMcpError body.

security.trustModel: The daemon has no authentication; trust is same-user access to a local Unix socket. coven-mcp narrows that authority before an LLM touches it.

controls.detail: Unset or empty allowlist means every write tool is denied.
Any invalid allowlist entry aborts startup, naming the entry position but never its value.
send_input and kill_session authorize the daemon's own project_root, never a caller-supplied path.
Containment is path-component based after symlink resolution, so /work/app2 is never inside /work/app.
Missing paths, symlink escapes, dot-dot traversal, dead directories, and lookup failures all deny.
Memory excerpts blank by default; revealRequired or any non-public classification forces redaction even when enabled.
Prompts, input, output, excerpts, env values, tokens, and raw daemon bodies are never logged. Stdout is exclusively JSON-RPC.

explicitNonGuarantees: The allowlist is an authorization gate, not a process sandbox; a launched harness keeps full same-user OS authority.
Tool results are untrusted content with respect to prompt injection. Encoding is sanitized; meaning is not.
Resume tokens are integrity-protected but not encrypted, and carry un-emitted output state.
Anyone with same-user access can bypass coven-mcp by talking to the daemon directly.

outputPipeline.problem: Daemon events carry raw PTY bytes: ANSI escapes, carriage-return rewrites, C0/C1 controls, lines split across events, and payloads double-encoded as JSON strings.

sanitizer.model: Terminal state machine with eight states (ground, escape, charset, csi, osc, oscEsc, str, strEsc).
sanitizer.emitsOn: newline reached in ground state, so a split escape sequence can never leak
sanitizer.carriageReturn: overwrite from line start, so progress bars collapse to their final visible state
sanitizer.pendingState: compacted (current line buffer plus any in-progress escape), never accumulated raw history

resumeToken.restartBehavior: intentionally invalid after restart; recover with afterSeq = last observed lastSeq

invariants: An event is consumed only after its emitted text and pending state both fit the budget (try-before-commit).
A terminal session completes only after one further drain returns empty, so racing trailing output is not dropped.
An error never discards text already produced in the same call.

errorCodes.meaning: Socket unreachable, or the request timed out.
The daemon does not advertise a required capability.
Any other daemon error; carries the upstream code and status in safe details.
The session exists but is not running.
Input failed validation, named by field.
Token malformed, expired with the process, or bound to another session.
Output exceeds the text or pending-state bounds; details carry a usable token.

limits.name: HEALTH_CACHE_TTL_MS
limits.applies: health gate cache, success and failure alike

limits.name: DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS
limits.applies: per-request response, also bounded by the call deadline

configuration.purpose: Explicit daemon socket path, overriding discovery.
Colon-separated absolute project roots permitting write tools. Unset or empty means read-only.
Exactly the literal 'true' to forward bounded memory excerpts.

stages.proves: Biome lint and format across src, test, and scripts.
155 unit and contract tests against a real HTTP server on a temporary Unix socket.
Production build yields a runnable entry point.
Stdout purity, stable discovery with the daemon down, non-zero exit on misconfiguration.
Tarball contents, shebang, bin, and engines.
Required README sections present, non-empty, and in the submission guide's order.

supportingScripts.role: Deterministic demo against a scripted stand-in daemon.
Raw JSON-RPC smoke test of the built binary.
Real HTTP server bound to a temporary Unix socket.

nonGoals.reason: No push transport exists on the daemon socket; coven-relay accepts the WebSocket upgrade and closes.
coven-memory is a separate binary unreachable over the socket.
Exactly one action id exists today.
coven claim is CLI-only; there is no API route.
